scope: CBSE Class 6 Social Science · Exploring Society: India and Beyond · Chapter 3 · Landforms and Life
claimBoundary: This is deterministic readiness validation using synthetic learner scenarios. It is not a live student study, school pilot, efficacy trial, attainment claim, accessibility certification, or school-specific pacing validation.
passRule: Every scenario must map to an implemented Chapter 3 topic, a Kiki misconception/remediation path, at least one linked required assessment type, a privacy-safe learner action, and an observable mastery criterion.

scenarios.need: Learner classifies major landforms from a single visible cue, for example calling every high area a mountain or every broad area a plain.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: major landforms classified from one cue instead of multiple observable features
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare fictional profile cards using relative height, slope and broad-surface clues, then justify whether each example is best described as a mountain, plateau, plain or needs more evidence.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Independently classifies two unfamiliar major landforms using at least two relevant features and states when the evidence is insufficient for a confident label.

scenarios.need: Learner assumes every landscape must fit one rigid landform category and cannot reason about a mixed landscape containing more than one feature.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: mixed landscape forced into one absolute category
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Sort fictional mixed-landscape descriptions into dominant landform, mixed features or needs-more-evidence groups, explaining which clues support each choice without using personal location information.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly handles two unfamiliar mixed landscape cases without forcing a single absolute category when the description contains meaningful features of more than one landform.

scenarios.need: Learner makes deterministic claims that people living in mountains must have the same occupation, transport, housing or culture.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: mountain setting treated as a rule that determines human choices
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare two fictional mountain communities with different access, services and livelihood choices, then identify constraints and possibilities while explicitly separating geographic influence from human decisions.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Explains in two new mountain examples that landform can influence opportunities and constraints but does not determine occupation, culture or community choices.

scenarios.need: Learner assumes all mountain routes and settlements face identical access, weather or risk conditions simply because both are in mountainous terrain.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: all mountain places treated as having identical conditions
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare fictional valley, pass and slope scenarios with different season, route and service information, then make conditional statements about access without requesting live GPS or a learner's real location.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Uses evidence from two unfamiliar mountain scenarios to make conditional access comparisons and avoids stereotypes or universal claims about all mountain communities.

scenarios.need: Learner assumes every plateau contains the same minerals, soil, water availability or livelihood opportunities.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: all plateaus treated as having identical resources and livelihoods
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare fictional plateau evidence cards with different soil, water, mineral and transport information, and write only the resource or livelihood claims that the supplied evidence supports.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Distinguishes two unfamiliar plateau cases using the given evidence and avoids claiming that every plateau has the same resources, minerals or livelihoods.

scenarios.need: Learner assumes that finding a useful resource on a plateau automatically means it should be extracted or used without considering trade-offs.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: resource presence treated as automatic permission or benefit without trade-off reasoning
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use a fictional plateau decision matrix to compare possible resource benefits with water, land, community and environmental trade-offs, then state what additional evidence would be needed before a decision.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Produces a balanced evidence-aware response for two unfamiliar resource scenarios and explains why resource presence alone does not determine the best community decision.

scenarios.need: Learner states that all plains are fertile and safe, or that living close to a river is always beneficial without considering flood and drainage risk.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: plain and river advantages turned into universal fertility or safety claims
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare fictional plain and floodplain descriptions using soil, drainage, river and flood-history clues, then identify both opportunities and risks and propose a simple flood-aware adaptation.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Explains two unfamiliar plains or river cases conditionally, identifying both possible benefits and flood or drainage risks without claiming that all plains are fertile or safe.

scenarios.need: Learner needs a low-bandwidth, offline and instruction-light path for landform reasoning that does not depend on live maps, GPS, microphone, camera, cloud AI or personal-data collection.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use cached text, locally drawn fictional landform profiles and local assessment prompts; complete one Kiki step at a time without network-dependent tutoring, live GPS or disclosure of a home address.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Completes one plains-and-rivers adaptation task and its mastery check using local resources only, with no personal data, live location or remote service dependency.
